findings.summary: Clean designed no-op: at 16:52:57Z the watchdog found ≥1 non-completed runtime-loop.yml run among the last 30 (the Runtime chain was active) and exited before any dispatch — duplicate-suppression working as intended.

Guard policy executed but not exercised beyond the first branch: refuses fresh progression when the latest runtime-loop run concluded non-success ('REVISE router/watchdog/manual evidence must resolve it'); checks lab/runtime state/runtime_loop.json continue flag; computes next cycle_index as successful-run-count+1. All of this is durable workflow source at the pinned head_sha — nothing new over Git.

Latent coupling worth one infra glance: cycle_index for the next dispatch = count of completed-successful runs in the last 100 (gh run list window). The repo's own hygiene incidents deleted 102+21 runs; if a supervisor's counting window ever slides across a deletion boundary, dispatched cycle_index values can repeat or skip relative to lane state. Unverified whether downstream consumes cycle_index semantically; flagging the interaction only — status reflects the durable source mechanism, the deletion-interaction itself is an unverified curator inference.
~7s wall, zero model calls, zero writes — negligible orchestration overhead per firing.

research_opportunities: If supervisor logs are pruned by design (as the 102-run hygiene incident already did for this class), dispatch/cancel attributions become unprovable after the fact; committing one-line receipts (like program-supervisor.yml already does) would make even no-op firings auditable cheaply.
